note: Predeclared source-supported interpretations for the three fsm81 design-decision cases. Each source explicitly states "Final decision: fsm81 adopts option C" with a concrete named export / state change. Score ONLY these source-stated facts; do NOT credit options A/B (explicitly rejected by the source) or any final design decision the source does not state.

interpretations.supported_fact: fsm81 log retention adopts option C: the fixture file is append-only and the drain tool owns retention (the fixture never deletes/truncates a line). The fixture exposes only an append function and a read-back helper; the read-back helper is exported from fsm.js under the name lastLogLine and must return the last complete line without modifying the file.

fsm81 terminal-state modeling adopts option C: a single explicit state map where each state owns its complete event vocabulary and the machine object remains a pure input to every transition call. The failed state gains an explicit done event that settles to a terminal done state with no outgoing events.
not_supported: option A (fold done into failed with a flag)
option B (separate settlement event stream / second module)

interpretations.supported_fact: fsm81 export format adopts option C: a content-addressed manifest listing each tracked file with exact byte length and a short checksum (changed files marked changed, not copied); the bundle never embeds file contents. The manifest writer is exported from fsm.js under the name writeBundleManifest.
